summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and depression presented with acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and subjective fever. She had elevated liver enzymes, lactate, and transaminases with AST greater than ALT, concerning for mild alcoholic hepatitis and possible colitis. CT abdomen showed circumferential cecal wall thickening likely due to portal colopathy. Empiric antibiotics were started. Endoscopy revealed stable small esophageal varices and severe portal hypertensive gastropathy; a benign-appearing 5 mm polyp in the descending colon was removed. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, fluid resuscitation, and treatment of alcohol withdrawal. She was discharged home with improved pain, stable labs, and instructions to follow up on polyp biopsy, repeat EGD in one year, and hepatitis B vaccination.
